defs.def: to go to where sb/sth is and bring them/it back （去）拿来；（去）请来

ex.s: Dogs are known for their impressive fetching habit, but cats take this behavior up a notch.
ex.t: 狗以令人印象深刻的捡东西习惯闻名，但猫把这种行为更进了一步。

ex.s: fetch it at the SAC personally

So if we send out a robot with the single instruction of fetching coffee, it will have a strong desire to secure success by disabling its own off switch or even killing anyone who might interfere with its task.
ex.t: 所以，如果我们派出一个只接到“去取咖啡”这一指令的机器人，它会强烈渴望通过 disable 自己的关闭开关、甚至杀死任何可能干扰其任务的人来确保成功。

ex.s: A vacuum cleaner also comes in handy for fetching items that are floating around out-of-reach!
ex.t: 吸尘器也可以用来取漂浮在够不着的地方的物品！

ex.s: My niece came in to fetch something, maybe her handkerchief, apparently without seeing me.
ex.t: 我的侄女进来拿东西，也许是她的手帕，显然没有看见我。

ex.s: REFLECTING fetch superior to calculate have an urge to suspend dismiss explode pace 1 Batteries are not allowed by airlines in checked luggage, as they might due to overheating.
ex.t: 反映取货优势以计算有暂停解除爆炸步伐的冲动1航空公司不允许在托运行李中放置电池，因为它们可能是由于过热造成的。

ex.s: Then she went to fetch her neighbor, Mr Behrman, to be a model for her drawing.
ex.t: 然后她去请她的邻居贝尔曼先生来给她当画的模特。

ex.s: I returned to the car and fetched more possessions.
ex.t: 我回到车里，拿了更多的物品。

defs.def: to be sold for a particular price 售得，卖得（某价）
